promise: A buyer becomes a vendor from /become-a-vendor and, in Open registration mode, is selling immediately.
ux_bar: Vendor-only sections (Services, Sales, Earnings) appear without a reload or re-login, and the become-vendor CTA disappears from every surface that showed it.

promise: In Approval mode a new vendor is pending and cannot list or sell until an admin approves.

entry_points.api: POST wpss/v1/vendors/register; status change is admin-only

ux_bar: A pending vendor sees a clear 'awaiting approval' state - not the active vendor sections, and not a bare 'not a vendor' error that reads as a bug.

promise: A logged-out visitor can create an account inline without leaving the registration page and is signed in immediately.
ux_bar: Field-level errors (invalid email, weak password, already registered) appear NEXT TO the specific input, not only as a top banner; success redirects straight to the dashboard with no second login step.

promise: A vendor edits avatar, tagline, bio, intro video and social links, and the change shows on their public profile.
ux_bar: Avatar upload shows an instant local preview before the save completes, and falls back to the account Gravatar rather than a broken image when none is set.

promise: A vendor can pause new orders while staying published, with their own message shown to buyers (Vacation Mode).
ux_bar: Services stay visible in the catalog and on the profile, but the order action is DISABLED with the vendor's message in its place - not a 404, and not a service that is still quietly orderable.
notes: Promise stated verbatim in readme.txt - a marketing claim the catalog must hold us to.

promise: Anyone can open a vendor's public profile and see bio, stats, tier badge, portfolio, services and reviews.
ux_bar: The tier badge uses the same markup and colour class as on the vendor card in listings - the same vendor is never badged two different ways on two surfaces.

promise: A logged-in visitor can message a vendor from the public profile or a service page before ordering.
ux_bar: A logged-out visitor sees a login prompt rather than a form that fails on submit. The vendor receives a real email. On success the form is replaced by a CENTRED tick and confirmation block (48px circled tick, 12px gap) - on BOTH the service page and the vendor profile.
notes: 1.7.2 (cc657fe2): the success state had NO stylesheet rule at all on the vendor profile, because the only rule lived in single-service.css which does not load there. Class of defect: markup emitted with no rule in a sheet enqueued on that surface.

promise: A visitor can browse a directory of vendors to find a seller rather than a service.
ux_bar: An empty directory shows a designed empty state, not a blank grid. Suspended and pending vendors NEVER appear in the public listing.

promise: A vendor adds, edits and deletes portfolio items up to a configured maximum.
ux_bar: The Add button is DISABLED WITH A STATED REASON once wpss_max_portfolio_items (default 50) is reached, rather than accepting the submit and erroring server-side.

promise: A vendor reorders portfolio items by dragging and can feature a limited number.
ux_bar: Reordering persists without a page reload. Featuring beyond wpss_max_featured_portfolio (default 6) is REFUSED with a message rather than silently swapping out an existing featured item.

promise: A vendor can see their current tier and how close they are to the next one.

entry_points.frontend: MISSING - only a static badge, no progress anywhere

ux_bar: DEAD ON WEB. A vendor near a threshold should see a stated distance ('3 more 5-star orders to reach Pro'), not a badge that changes with no visible cause. Today they learn of a change only from an email.
notes: Verified 2026-09-19: route registered at src/API/SellerLevelsController.php:71; zero callers in templates/ or assets/js/.

promise: A suspended vendor is blocked from every selling action consistently, not just on some surfaces.

entry_points.api: wpss_rest_require_vendor() consults wpss_vendor_status_block() on every vendor-gated write

ux_bar: One consistent wpss_not_vendor outcome everywhere - never 403 on one route and full access on another.
notes: Eight private copies of this check had drifted before 1.7.0; a suspended vendor kept full REST access.

promise: A vendor starts a service with title, description and category in step 1.
ux_bar: Required fields validate INLINE before step 2 is reachable, rather than failing only at final publish.
notes: Two authoring surfaces for one outcome (wizard + wp-admin editor) - historically the most-reported area.

promise: A vendor sets a starting price and may optionally add Standard and Premium tiers.
ux_bar: A service using ONLY Basic can be published - a switched-off tier is never validated and its empty fields are never reported against Basic. A tier that IS switched on but left empty is refused, in the SAME words, on the Pricing step and at Publish. The review step omits disabled tiers rather than showing empty cards.
notes: 1.7.2 (931a4bbb, be71faee): disabled tiers leaked into wpss_validate_service_publishable() and their empty fields were reported against Basic, so a Basic-only service could not be published. Pricing step and Publish now share one pricingErrors().

promise: A vendor uploads a main image, gallery images and an optional video, up to configured limits.
ux_bar: The uploader disables at wpss_service_max_gallery (default 4) with a limit notice, rather than accepting images the review step silently drops. Selecting an image ALREADY in the gallery is refused with 'That image is already in your gallery.' and leaves no empty tile. Opening a service whose saved gallery contains a repeated id hydrates deduplicated with no console error.
notes: 1.7.2 (6f1a2a7d): the strip is an x-for keyed on image.id, so a duplicate key made Alpine THROW ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading after)') and leave orphaned empty tiles. It also locked vendors out of editing a service already saved with a duplicate. Not visible on the public page, which dedupes - which is why the card read as unconfirmed.

promise: A vendor defines custom requirement fields (text, number, yes/no, date, file, select, multiple-choice), each required or optional.
ux_bar: The wizard's type dropdown offers the SAME full set, with the SAME labels, as the wp-admin metabox - driven from one shared map, never two lists that can drift.
notes: Basecamp 10286129293: the wizard offered 4 of 8 types and mislabelled select vs radio. Now one wpss_requirement_type_labels().

promise: A vendor adds paid add-ons and FAQs up to configured limits.
ux_bar: Price fields use the same numeric step/format as the pricing step so a vendor cannot type a value checkout will reject. Remove controls on extras, FAQs, deliverables and gallery images have accessible names, and icons on a row added dynamically RENDER without a reload. Removing one row must not corrupt the values of the others.
notes: 1.7.2 (41e0200c): Lucide icons hydrate once at page load, so dynamically added rows rendered iconless until refreshIcons() was added at 5 call sites; 6 icon-only buttons gained aria-labels; 10 x-model bindings were rebound from data.extras[index].x to extra.x to kill stale-index errors.

promise: A vendor reviews a full summary of every step before publishing.
ux_bar: A checklist item reads complete ONLY when the underlying data is actually present server-side - never from client state alone when that step's save failed.

promise: A vendor can save an in-progress service and resume later without losing data.
ux_bar: Reopening restores the wizard to the step it was left on with every field populated - not reset to step 1 with the data only in the database.

promise: A vendor edits an existing service through the same wizard used to create it.
ux_bar: Opening another vendor's edit URL directly gives an explicit permission message - never a wizard that loads blank or, worse, someone else's data.

promise: A vendor is told the service limit before hitting it, and refused with a message rather than a silent failure.

entry_points.frontend: dashboard/services limit notice; create blocked with a message
entry_points.admin: Settings > Vendor > Max services per vendor
entry_points.api: wpss_vendor_can_create_service checked on POST /services and the wizard save

ux_bar: The list states the limit in the vendor's own numbers ('2 of 3') BEFORE they hit it, not only as an error afterwards. A site owner acting as a vendor is never blocked by their own paywall.
notes: 0 means unlimited.

promise: A vendor is told the tag limit and refused, rather than having extra tags silently dropped on save.
ux_bar: The hint STATES the maximum, and exceeding it is refused with a message. Extras are never accepted by the form and then discarded at save time.
notes: 1.7.2 (0fa4cda1): max_tags added to wpss_get_service_limits() with a wpss_service_max_tags filter, enforced on both save paths, surfaced in the hint and a validationTags message. Previously the form accepted any number and the save silently dropped the overflow.

promise: With moderation on, a new or edited service is held pending and hidden from the catalog until approved - however it was published.
ux_bar: The gate holds on EVERY publish path - the dashboard wizard, the wp-admin editor and REST alike. A vendor is emailed and shown the pending state immediately, rather than discovering it by noticing the service is missing.
notes: 1.7.2 (a59224df, 265ce4df): the guards registered inside define_admin_hooks(), which early-returns on REST because is_admin() is false there - so publishing from the dashboard bypassed moderation entirely. Guards moved to ServiceModerationPage::register_guards() called from a new define_moderation_hooks(). A one-time migration returns already-published-unapproved services to the queue.

promise: With moderation off (default), a published service goes live immediately.
ux_bar: The publish button's label and the resulting state agree - the service appears on the public archive in the cycle a vendor would expect, not delayed by an uninvalidated cache.

promise: A vendor whose service is rejected sees the admin's reason and can edit and resubmit.

roles.vendor: can see own reason and resubmit

ux_bar: A rejected service is visually DISTINCT from an ordinary draft (its own Rejected label), so the vendor does not have to guess why it never went live.

promise: A vendor's Services list shows every service with its real status and per-status counts.
ux_bar: Zero services shows a designed empty state with a 'Create your first service' action, not a bare '0 services'. Counts add up to the list below them (rejected excluded from the draft bucket).

promise: A buyer saves services via a heart and can unfavorite from the dashboard without a reload.
ux_bar: Unfavoriting removes the card immediately, and the list paginates at 20/page so a long list never loads every row.

promise: A buyer posts a job request for vendors to propose against.
ux_bar: The posted request appears in the buyer's own list and the public archive in the same session, without a manual refresh to confirm it saved.

promise: A buyer manages their own requests - view proposals, edit an open one, or close it.
ux_bar: A request that already converted to an order is READ-ONLY, rather than letting the buyer edit terms an accepted proposal already committed to.

promise: A vendor browses open requests and submits a proposal on one they can fulfil.
ux_bar: A vendor cannot submit a SECOND proposal on the same request without withdrawing the first - the form reflects their existing proposal rather than silently allowing duplicates. A vendor proposing on their own request is blocked.
notes: Self-dealing guard called out in ROLE_MATRIX.md.

promise: A vendor sees every proposal they sent with its outcome in one list.
ux_bar: A proposal lost because the buyer hired someone else reads 'Not selected'; one declined for another reason reads 'Declined'. The two are never conflated into one ambiguous label.
notes: New in 1.7.1 (Basecamp 10264294123) - before it, a vendor had no list of what they had bid on and learned of a loss only by reopening the request.

promise: A vendor can withdraw a proposal before it is accepted, from the place they manage proposals.
ux_bar: Once withdrawn the state is reflected on BOTH the buyer's request page and the vendor's proposals list, not only the page the action fired from. The action should live where the vendor manages proposals, not only on the original request.
notes: INCONSISTENT PLACEMENT: dashboard/proposals is read-only, so a vendor must navigate back to the original request to withdraw. Worth its own card.

promise: Buyer and vendor message each other about an order or request, with attachments, from a shared list.
ux_bar: The unread count is VISIBLE (a regression once hid it behind a text-indent trick) and clears when the thread opens; a closed order thread never keeps an unread badge. The attachment accept list matches the order composer's exactly.

promise: A member sees their notifications, can reach older ones, and can mark one or all read or delete one - identically on every surface that shows the list.

entry_points.frontend: dashboard/notifications, standalone account page, WooCommerce myaccount (one shared partial)

ux_bar: Paginated at 20/page with working prev/next; the OLDEST notification is reachable, and an out-of-range page clamps to the last real page rather than rendering empty. All three surfaces render the same markup and the same mark-read behaviour.
notes: 1.7.2 (edae9435): the data layer and REST route were both paginated, but the template fetched a hardcoded 50 with no offset and rendered a flat list with no pager - so anything past the newest 50 was unreachable. Added wpss_count_user_notifications() (COUNT(*), not count of a full fetch) and a wpss_notifications_per_page filter.

promise: Any member can update their basic account profile, independent of vendor-only fields.
ux_bar: A plain buyer sees ONLY the fields relevant to them - vendor-only fields (tagline, bio, vacation mode) are not rendered and then rejected on save.

promise: A vendor sees available, pending and clearing balances separately, and can request a withdrawal once eligible.
ux_bar: The 'ready for withdrawal' banner appears only when available balance actually MEETS THE MINIMUM - not merely when balance is non-zero.
notes: Prior bug: any-earnings triggered the banner instead of available >= minimum, miscounting 4 of 8 vendors.

promise: A vendor views a ledger of wallet transactions, each linked back to the order or tip that caused it.
ux_bar: Each row's reference link OPENS the specific order or tip that caused the entry - a vendor auditing their balance never has to guess which order a debit belongs to.
notes: wallet and earnings are deliberately one template, not a duplicate.

promise: A vendor on Free opening Analytics sees a clear Pro message rather than a blank page or an error.

entry_points.api: n/a - no Free route backs it

roles.vendor: sees the upsell, not the feature

ux_bar: The message matches the site's ACTUAL state: 'part of WP Sell Services Pro' when Pro is inactive, versus a generic 'not available' only if Pro is active but the section is still absent. Never the wrong message for the install.
notes: 'analytics' is in VENDOR_SECTIONS with a nav title but the Free template does not exist; render_section_fallback() catches this deliberately. Documented Pro gate, not a defect.

promise: A buyer or vendor can open a dispute on an eligible order within the configured window.

entry_points.frontend: dashboard/disputes or order view Open Dispute

ux_bar: Once the window has passed the control is NOT SHOWN at all, rather than shown and then rejected. The reason list matches wpss_dispute_reasons exactly on both the open form and the admin view.

promise: Both parties add messages and evidence to an open dispute in a thread visible to each other and the admin.
ux_bar: The add-evidence form DISAPPEARS once the dispute is resolved or closed. An attachment shows its real original filename, never a numeric attachment ID.

promise: A dispute escalates to admin review if the other party does not respond within the deadline.
ux_bar: Both original parties can SEE the escalation - it is never a silent behind-the-scenes status change with no notification of what happened to their case.
notes: Action Scheduler; wpss_dispute_reminder_days / wpss_dispute_auto_escalate_days control timing.

promise: The site owner resolves a dispute with a written resolution and, when warranted, an exact refund amount.
ux_bar: The refund field only matters when the resolution type authorises a refund, and a resolved dispute's resolution label RENDERS rather than fataling.
notes: 1.7.0: Dispute::get_resolution_label() called a method that exists only on DisputeService - a fatal on any resolved dispute that survived because nothing had called the accessor before.

promise: The dispute window setting has a real, enforced effect.
ux_bar: Changing the window from 14 to 3 immediately changes WHICH already-completed orders can still be disputed - the check is computed at open time against the completion date, not only applied to future orders.

promise: A buyer leaves a star rating and review on a completed order within the review window.
ux_bar: The form DISAPPEARS once wpss_review_window_days has elapsed, rather than accepting a submission the server rejects. A second review on the same order is impossible.

promise: A vendor can post a single public reply to a review they received.
ux_bar: Once a reply exists the form is REPLACED by the reply - no second reply can overwrite the first. /dashboard/reviews/ is directly reachable rather than redirecting to the dashboard landing page.
notes: New in 1.7.1: the order page told vendors to respond from their Reviews section since 1.2, while that section did not exist and the URL redirected away.

promise: A reader can mark a review helpful, once.
ux_bar: A second click from the same visitor is refused with a clear 'already marked' rather than double-counting or silently doing nothing with no feedback.
notes: Atomic UPDATE, safe under concurrent clicks.

promise: With review moderation on, a review is held pending and excluded from public display AND rating averages until decided.

roles.vendor: cannot see pending on own services

ux_bar: The cached average rating RECOMPUTES the moment a review is approved or rejected - never left stale until an unrelated event refreshes it.
notes: The rating cache was once written on create but never refreshed on moderation.

promise: The site owner sees actionable counts (open disputes, pending vendors, pending moderation) that link straight to the queue.
ux_bar: A card with zero items renders MUTED rather than the same alarming treatment as one with real items pending, so the owner's eye goes to what needs attention.

promise: The owner approves or rejects pending services individually or in bulk, with an optional reason emailed.
ux_bar: Confirmations use the shared wpssConfirm dialog, not the browser's native confirm(). The menu badge count matches the count on the page. A pending service is NEVER briefly visible publicly and then pulled.
notes: FEATURE_AUDIT.md records 5 remaining alert()/confirm() calls elsewhere in admin JS.

promise: The owner sees every vendor with key stats, filters by status, approves/suspends/reactivates, and overrides commission.
ux_bar: The vendor detail screen's tabs LOAD - including when the plugin's admin menu title has been renamed, which Pro white-label sells. A per-vendor commission override reset to blank falls back to the global rate everywhere earnings are computed, never a stale zero that gives that vendor 100%. Approving grants role and status in one action with no in-between state.
notes: 1.7.2 (abcd9855): the screen derived its hook suffix from the menu title, so renaming the menu (a Pro feature) left the tabs on 'Loading' forever. Now captured from add_submenu_page(). Cross-plugin config breakage - a whole class worth testing with white-label ON.

promise: The owner reviews payout requests, approves/rejects/marks paid, and exports the filtered list as CSV.

entry_points.frontend: vendor sees own history in dashboard/earnings

ux_bar: The CSV export NEVER mutates status as a side effect - exporting the same filter twice produces identical rows. Mark-paid is offered only on pending/approved rows. A double-click cannot double-debit (row-locked, idempotent).

promise: The owner sees a filterable, sortable list of every dispute and can act on several at once.
ux_bar: Status filter views show accurate per-status counts, and the list PAGINATES rather than loading every dispute the site has ever had.

promise: The owner sees every order with filters for status, date and sub-order type, sortable, with bulk actions.
ux_bar: The sub-order type filter lists only types actually PRESENT in the data, rather than always offering every possible type including ones with zero rows.

promise: The owner approves or rejects pending reviews and the rating average recomputes immediately.
ux_bar: Acting shows an inline toast without a full reload, and the status tab counts update to match. The link to the setting that controls this feature opens Settings AT the section holding it, not a generic tab.
notes: 1.7.2 (8e258a41): the settings link pointed at a generic page; now admin.php?page=wpss-settings#vendor.

promise: The owner sees user-filed reports against a service, vendor or review and resolves each, including changing the reported account's status.
ux_bar: The menu label carries a live open-report COUNT, so an owner who never opens the screen is not silently missing new reports - and the count runs a real COUNT(*), not a fetch-and-count.

promise: The owner can review a read-only history of system events, filterable by object, event, actor, date and forced-only.
ux_bar: Combining filters narrows to their INTERSECTION, matching the screen's own example ('every forced order status change in the last week').

promise: A first-time owner is guided through a short setup wizard and can revisit or re-run it later.

entry_points.admin: Sell Services > Setup Wizard, auto-redirect on activation

ux_bar: The wizard stays reachable AFTER completion, so an owner who left early is never permanently locked out. Completion is one flag written in one place, not inferred from partial state.

promise: The owner sets platform name, default currency, and which e-commerce platform owns checkout.

entry_points.frontend: name appears in emails and branding

ux_bar: Changing ecommerce_platform actually SWAPS which rail owns payment, and switching rails never rewrites past orders - historical orders keep working under the rail that created them.

promise: The owner maps which pages serve as Services, Dashboard, Cart, Checkout, Vendors, Become-a-Vendor and Terms, and is warned if Terms is unmapped while checkout is live.

entry_points.frontend: the mapped pages are what members navigate

ux_bar: The 'no Terms page mapped but buyers are paying' notice shows on every WPSS admin screen until a Terms page is chosen, and DISAPPEARS the moment one is, without a save-and-reload cycle to confirm.
notes: Documented intentional zero-config gap: a warning, not a checkout block.

promise: The owner enables Stripe, PayPal and/or Offline on the standalone rail, with credentials masked once saved.
ux_bar: A saved secret displays MASKED and is PRESERVED when the field is left empty on re-save - it is never blanked just because the owner saved the form without retyping it.
notes: wpss_render_secret_field() with keep-on-empty is the shared implementation.

promise: The owner sets the platform commission rate and tax for standalone checkout.

entry_points.frontend: reflected in checkout totals and vendor earnings

ux_bar: Changing the rate changes what a NEW order computes and never rewrites a past order's recorded commission. All commission maths routes through CommissionService::compute_breakdown() - one function, not a display copy.
notes: Tax applies to standalone checkout only; WooCommerce uses its own.

promise: The owner sets minimum withdrawal, the clearance hold after completion, and optional auto-withdrawal.
ux_bar: Raising the hold days immediately changes which already-completed orders count as available versus pending on the vendor's earnings page - visible on the next load, not only on future orders.
notes: A hold of 0 pays out as soon as an order completes.

promise: The owner controls vendor registration mode, max services per vendor, service moderation and review moderation.

entry_points.frontend: reflected in become-a-vendor and the publish gate

ux_bar: Switching registration from Open to Approval takes effect for the very next signup, does NOT retroactively re-pend active vendors, and needs no cache clear. Switching moderation ON must gate every publish path, not only wp-admin.
notes: See WIZ-10 - moderation previously did not gate the dashboard publish path at all.

promise: The owner controls auto-complete, whether disputes are allowed, vendor self-refund, dispute windows and requirements timeout.

entry_points.frontend: reflected in order actions and dispute eligibility

ux_bar: Toggling 'let vendors refund their own orders' immediately shows or hides the Refund action on the vendor's order view. Auto-complete only fires on an order where something was actually DELIVERED.
notes: Off by default because refunds reverse the vendor's own credit. 1.7.2 (57eb9009) tied auto-complete to a real delivery.

promise: The owner toggles which notification types send, and each toggle gates BOTH the email and the in-app notification.

entry_points.frontend: members set their own per-category preferences in their profile

ux_bar: Unchecking one type silences it on EVERY path it can fire from - not email-only while the in-app notification keeps appearing.
notes: 1.7.0: the type list existed twice and had drifted - notify_moderation was gated by EmailService but written by nothing in Settings, and TYPE_REVIEW_RECEIVED was missing from one map. Now one get_notification_types() with a contract test.
